def slugify_params(args: argparse.Namespace) -> dict[str, Any]:
    """Build the keyword arguments for :func:`slugify` from parsed CLI arguments.

    The parsed ``regex_pattern`` value is forwarded unchanged (including ``None``)
    so the CLI applies the same custom disallowed-character pattern as the library
    call. All other CLI options, positional/STDIN input, and case/Unicode behavior
    are preserved.
    """
    return dict(
        text=args.input_string,
        entities=args.entities,
        decimal=args.decimal,
        hexadecimal=args.hexadecimal,
        max_length=args.max_length,
        word_boundary=args.word_boundary,
        save_order=args.save_order,
        separator=args.separator,
        stopwords=args.stopwords,
        regex_pattern=args.regex_pattern,
        lowercase=args.lowercase,
        replacements=args.replacements,
        allow_unicode=args.allow_unicode
    )

from slugify import slugify
from slugify.__main__ import parse_args, slugify_params

def test_regex_forwarded_none():
    params = slugify_params(parse_args(['slugify', 'Hello']))
    assert params['regex_pattern'] is None
    assert slugify(**params) == 'hello'

def test_regex_forwarded_custom():
    pattern = r'[^a-z_]+'
    params = slugify_params(parse_args(['slugify', 'Hello_42', '--regex-pattern', pattern]))
    assert params['regex_pattern'] == pattern
    assert slugify(**params) == 'hello_'

def test_other_options_preserved():
    params = slugify_params(parse_args(['slugify', 'A B', '--separator', '_', '--no-lowercase']))
    assert params['separator'] == '_'
    assert params['lowercase'] is False
    assert params['regex_pattern'] is None
    assert slugify(**params) == 'A_B'

def test_iterable_options_still_work():
    reps = iter([('|', 'or'), iter(['%', 'percent'])])
    assert slugify('a|b%c', replacements=reps) == 'aorborpercent'
    sw = iter(['the'])
    assert slugify('the quick the', stopwords=sw) == 'quick'

:param stopwords (iterable): words to discount; one-shot iterables are consumed once
    :param regex_pattern (str): regex pattern for disallowed characters
    :param lowercase (bool): activate case sensitivity by setting it to False
    :param replacements (iterable): list of replacement rules e.g. [['|', 'or'], ['%', 'percent']];
        one-shot iterables, including one-shot rule iterables, are consumed once and applied in
        both the initial and final replacement passes with original rule order preserved
    :param allow_unicode (bool): allow unicode characters
    :return (str):
    """

    # materialize one-shot iterables so they can be used in both replacement passes
    if replacements is not None:
        replacements = [tuple(rule) for rule in replacements]
    if stopwords is not None:
        stopwords = list(stopwords)

    # user-specific replacements
    if replacements:
        for old, new in replacements:
            text = text.replace(old, new)

A finite stopwords iterable must behave like the equivalent list for both lowercase=True and lowercase=False, even when the first input word is not a stopword. from slugify import slugify

def test_iterables_in_both_passes_and_membership():
    assert slugify('a b', replacements=iter([('-', '+')])) == 'a+b'
    assert slugify('Keep Drop Tail', stopwords=iter(['Drop']), lowercase=False) == 'Keep-Tail'
import pytest
from slugify import slugify

class SingleUse:
    def __init__(self, values): self.values = values; self.used = False
    def __iter__(self):
        if self.used: raise AssertionError('iterable consumed twice')
        self.used = True
        yield from self.values

def test_private_nested_one_shot_rules():
    rules = SingleUse([SingleUse(('-', '+')), SingleUse(('+', 'x'))])
    assert slugify('a b', replacements=rules) == 'axb'

@pytest.mark.parametrize('lowercase, expected', [(True, 'keep-tail'), (False, 'Keep-Tail')])
def test_private_stopword_consumption(lowercase, expected):
    words = SingleUse(['Drop'])
    assert slugify('Keep Drop Tail Drop', stopwords=words, lowercase=lowercase) == expected

def test_private_rule_order_and_caller_lists():
    rules = [['-', '+'], ['+', 'x']]
    stops = ['Drop']
    assert slugify('Keep Drop Tail', replacements=rules, stopwords=stops, lowercase=False) == 'KeepxTail'
    assert rules == [['-', '+'], ['+', 'x']]
    assert stops == ['Drop']

def test_private_none_empty_and_composed_options():
    assert slugify('À B', replacements=None, stopwords=None) == 'a-b'
    assert slugify('À B', replacements=iter(()), stopwords=iter(())) == 'a-b'
    expected = slugify('À foo B C', stopwords=['foo'], replacements=[('-', '+')], allow_unicode=True, separator=':', max_length=4)
    actual = slugify('À foo B C', stopwords=SingleUse(['foo']), replacements=SingleUse([SingleUse(('-', '+'))]), allow_unicode=True, separator=':', max_length=4)
    assert actual == expected
